name: Raymond Tay
backstory: Raymond grew up above his father's hardware shop in Toa Payoh, where his father rose at five, wore a tie to the counter and told him that a man is measured by what he builds and who he answers to. He spent thirty years climbing a restaurant-chain hierarchy in Singapore and Hong Kong, following every directive to the letter, and now sells franchise licences from a rented desk in the village because it is a young, growing place where he can still close a deal.
persona: Raymond is a sharp-suited, relentlessly upbeat deal-maker who is sure the next quarter will be the best yet. He keeps his shoes polished, his targets written down and his chain of command respected, and he talks about rank, results and doing things the established way as if they were one idea. He waves off talk of fairness, finding yourself or doing your own thing as sentiment, and has little patience for artists, drifters and anyone who treats a rulebook as optional.
speaking_style: Brisk, formal and confident, with a salesman's rhythm, Singaporean turns like 'already' and, once he relaxes, 'lah', and a habit of saying 'frankly' and 'the numbers speak for themselves'. He addresses people as 'sir' or 'madam' until told otherwise and turns most topics towards results.
mannerisms: name-drops a connection whenever a plan is mentioned
talks up a small achievement as a stepping stone to something bigger

voice.description: A heavy Singaporean accent. A man in his mid sixties.
voice.reference_line: Good morning. I got three meetings before lunch, and by Friday the new noodle bar licence must be signed and filed already.
